name: Insulin detemir
summary: A long-acting basal insulin whose action is prolonged by albumin binding; duration is dose-dependent and often requires twice-daily dosing.
mechanism: Acylation of insulin with myristic acid promotes reversible albumin binding, slowing absorption and prolonging action to give basal coverage.
pharmacodynamics: Provides relatively flat background insulin with less between-patient variability than NPH; weight gain signal may be lower than NPH.

pharmacokinetics.metabolism: Enzymatic degradation; hepatic and renal clearance

dosing.adult: Individualized; once or twice daily SC (often BID in type 1 diabetes), typically about 30–50% of total daily insulin as basal

safety.pregnancy: Safe and standard; insulin is the preferred glucose-lowering treatment in pregnancy
safety.lactation: Generally safe; insulin does not cross into breast milk in significant amounts
warnings: Hypoglycemia, especially with missed meals or exercise
Dose-dependent duration means coverage may wane before 24 h
monitoring: Blood glucose (including fasting and pre-dinner if BID)
safety.overdose: Hypoglycemia; treat with oral or IV glucose and close monitoring

clinicalPearls: Its duration is dose-dependent — at lower doses it may not last a full 24 h, so T1DM patients are often dosed twice daily.
Some trials suggest less weight gain with detemir than NPH insulin.
good: Relatively flat basal profile with a lower weight-gain signal than NPH.
bad: Coverage may not span 24 h at low doses; BID dosing is common in type 1 diabetes.
